claims.assertion: In FY2025, revenue attributed to Singapore by customer billing location was $23,684m (18% of total), while shipments to Singapore were under 2% of total revenue.
claims.pinpoint: 10-K FY2025, Note 17 geographic table and footnote (1)
claims.supporting_passage: "Singapore represented 18% of fiscal year 2025 total revenue based upon customer billing location. Customers use Singapore to centralize invoicing while our products are almost always shipped elsewhere. Shipments to Singapore were less than 2% of fiscal year 2025 total revenue."
claims.scope: NVIDIA consolidated revenue, FY ended 26 Jan 2025; geography by billing location
excluded_implications: That Singapore-billed revenue was destined for China
That Singapore-billed revenue was destined for Singapore
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Billing centralization by multinational (including U.S.) customers is the company's stated explanation.

claims.assertion: At least about $21.1bn of FY2025 revenue was billed to Singapore but shipped elsewhere (23,684 − <2% × 130,497 = 23,684 − <2,610).
claims.supporting_passage: Derived from SI1-C-01 inputs and total revenue $130,497m
excluded_implications: Any statement about the actual destinations of that revenue
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The <2% figure is an upper bound, so the residual is a lower bound.

claims.assertion: For Q1 and Q2 FY2026, NVIDIA stated that over 99% of controlled Data Center compute revenue billed to Singapore was for orders from U.S.-based customers; Singapore-billed revenue was $9,017m (20%) and $10,156m (22%).
claims.pinpoint: 10-Q Q1 FY2026 and Q2 FY2026, revenue-by-geography note, footnote (1)
claims.supporting_passage: "Over 99% of controlled Data Center compute revenue billed to Singapore was for orders from U.S.-based customers."
claims.scope: Controlled products meeting ECCN 3A090.a / 4A090.a; Q1–Q2 FY2026
excluded_implications: That the end users or physical destinations were in the U.S.
That non-controlled products follow the same pattern
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: 'U.S.-based customers' describes the ordering party; downstream resale, deployment location and remote access by third parties are not addressed.

claims.assertion: From Q3 FY2026 NVIDIA changed geographic revenue attribution from customer billing location to customer headquarters and recast prior periods; the Singapore line no longer appears.
claims.pinpoint: 10-Q Q3 FY2026 geographic note footnote (1); 10-K FY2026 Note 16 footnote (1)
claims.supporting_passage: "Previously, revenue by geographic area was reported based on the billing location of our customers, which often reflected a customer's centralized invoicing location, even though our products were almost always shipped elsewhere."
claims.scope: Disclosure basis from Q3 FY2026 onward
excluded_implications: That the change was made to conceal anything
That the change altered reported totals
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The company's stated rationale is a 'better representation of the geographic profile'. Either basis leaves end-use location undisclosed except for the Taiwan footnote.

claims.assertion: Both bases disclaim end-use: 'The end customer and shipping location may be different from our customers' headquarters location.'
claims.supporting_passage: "The end customer and shipping location may be different from our customers' headquarters location."
excluded_implications: That end-customer location differs materially (only that it may)

claims.assertion: FY2026 revenue by customer HQ: U.S. $149,617m; Taiwan $42,345m; China (incl. Hong Kong) $19,677m; Other $4,299m; total $215,938m. NVIDIA estimates 76% of Data Center revenue from Taiwan-headquartered customers was attributed to end customers in the U.S. and Europe.
claims.pinpoint: 10-K FY2026 Note 16 geographic table and footnote (2)
claims.supporting_passage: "In fiscal year 2026, we estimate 76% of Data Center revenue from Taiwan-headquartered customers was attributed to end customers based in the United States and Europe."
excluded_implications: That the remaining 24% went to China
Any split of Taiwan-HQ revenue between Data Center and other segments
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The residual 24% includes Taiwan, other Asia, the Middle East and elsewhere.

claims.assertion: Upper bound only: Taiwan-HQ Data Center revenue attributed to end customers outside the U.S. and Europe was at most about $10.2bn in FY2026 (24% × $42,345m, treating all Taiwan-HQ revenue as Data Center, which overstates the base).
excluded_implications: A China-specific figure
A point estimate
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The Data Center share of Taiwan-HQ revenue is not disclosed; the true figure is lower by an unknown amount.

claims.assertion: China (incl. Hong Kong) HQ revenue: first half FY2026 $13,644m combined; Q3 $2,973m; Q4 $3,060m (derived: 19,677 − 16,617).
excluded_implications: That residual ~$3bn/quarter China-HQ revenue is Data Center compute
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The company says it was effectively foreclosed from China data-center compute, so the residual is likely other segments or networking, but the filings do not split it.

claims.assertion: The April 2025 H20 licence requirement produced a $4.5bn charge; licensed H20 sales later generated about $60m; an H200 licence (Feb 2026) had produced no revenue; NVIDIA states it was 'effectively foreclosed' from China's data-center compute market at FY2026 year-end.
claims.pinpoint: 8-K 15 Apr 2025 Item 8.01; 10-K FY2026 Item 1 and Item 1A (export controls)
claims.supporting_passage: "As of the end of fiscal year 2026, we were effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market"
excluded_implications: That China-linked demand for NVIDIA products ceased
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Foreclosure describes NVIDIA's direct, licensed participation; it does not address indirect demand outside China-HQ customers.

claims.assertion: The Q1 FY2027 outlook ($78.0bn ± 2%) assumed no Data Center compute revenue from China.
claims.supporting_passage: "We are not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in our outlook."
claims.scope: Q1 FY2027 outlook as of 25 Feb 2026
excluded_implications: What sell-side consensus assumed
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Company guidance is evidence of the company's stated assumption, not of market expectations.

claims.assertion: NVIDIA identified reports of diversion as a business risk even when unsubstantiated, and disclosed that a substantial portion of products are warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong.
claims.supporting_passage: "reports of diversion of controlled products, even when unsubstantiated and untrue, may negatively impact our business, relationships with partners and customers, and our reputation"; "a substantial portion of our products, which are warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong"
excluded_implications: That diversion occurred
That NVIDIA was aware of any specific diversion
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Risk-factor language is precautionary and broad.

claims.assertion: Export-control licence conditions already limit foreign firms' ability to offer large GPU clusters as a service, i.e. cloud access is itself a regulated channel distinct from chip ownership.
claims.supporting_passage: "the USG already imposed license conditions that limit the ability of foreign firms to create and offer as a service large-scale GPU clusters"
claims.scope: U.S. export-control licence conditions, as described by NVIDIA
excluded_implications: That any specific provider offered compute to Chinese users

claims.assertion: Revenue concentration: one direct customer was 22% and another 14% of FY2026 revenue (Compute & Networking).
claims.supporting_passage: "sales to one direct customer represented 22% of total revenue and sales to another direct customer represented 14% of total revenue"
excluded_implications: The identities of these customers

claims.assertion: FY2026 Data Center revenue $193,737m (compute $162,361m; networking $31,376m); gross margin 71.1% (75.0% in FY2025).
claims.supporting_passage: Data Center 193,737; Compute 162,361; Networking 31,376; 'Gross margins decreased to 71.1% in fiscal year 2026 from 75.0%'
excluded_implications: Margin on any specific channel

claims.assertion: Singapore's trade ministry stated that physical deliveries of Nvidia products to Singapore were under 1% of Nvidia's revenue, that the rest of the revenue billed to Singapore entities involved no physical shipment into Singapore, and that Singapore has no legal obligation to enforce other countries' unilateral export controls.
claims.supporting_passage: "physical delivery of products sold by Nvidia to Singapore represent less than 1% of Nvidia's overall revenue"; "While we currently do not have legal obligations to enforce the unilateral export controls of other countries"
excluded_implications: That Singapore entities violated U.S. law
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Singapore states it will act against deceptive or dishonest practices under its own laws.

claims.assertion: On 13 May 2025 BIS announced rescission of the AI Diffusion Rule, diversion-tactics guidance to industry, and 'additional export licensing requirements for exports of SI chips to Malaysia and Thailand, due to known instances of diversion'.
claims.supporting_passage: "Imposing additional export licensing requirements for exports of SI chips to Malaysia and Thailand, due to known instances of diversion."
excluded_implications: That a final rule with that content was in force by the cutoff (not verified in this prototype)
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The press release states an intention; the implementing rule text was not retrieved.

claims.assertion: From 14 July 2025 Malaysia requires a Strategic Trade Permit for all exports, transshipments and transits of high-performance AI chips of U.S. origin, under the catch-all provision of section 12 of the Strategic Trade Act 2010.
claims.supporting_passage: "effective immediately, all exports, tranships and transits of high-performance AI chips of US origin are subject to a Strategic Trade Permit"
excluded_implications: That the permit regime covers in-country deployment or remote (cloud) access
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The measure targets physical outbound movement; chips installed in Malaysian data centres and accessed remotely are not addressed by its text.

claims.assertion: DOJ charged U.S. citizens and Chinese nationals with exporting NVIDIA GPUs to the PRC through Malaysia and Thailand between September 2023 and November 2025 (400 A100 exported; H100/H200 attempts disrupted).
claims.supporting_passage: "illegally exporting advanced GPUs to the PRC through Malaysia and Thailand"; "An indictment is merely an allegation and every defendant is presumed innocent"
claims.scope: U.S. federal case, M.D. Fla.; allegation stage
excluded_implications: That NVIDIA was involved or aware
That the routing scale is material to NVIDIA revenue
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The volumes in this case are small relative to NVIDIA revenue; it evidences the mechanism (U.S.-based reseller → Southeast Asia → PRC), not its magnitude.

claims.assertion: By 14 October 2025 a U.S. Senator had publicly named Megaspeed (Singapore) as an alleged diversion channel, relaying reports that its NVIDIA purchases equalled 'nearly two percent of worldwide datacenter sales last year', that chips moved through Malaysia and Singapore, and that Megaspeed stopped ordering after Malaysian and Singaporean crackdowns in mid-2025; he asked Commerce to investigate.
claims.supporting_passage: "This totaled nearly two percent of worldwide datacenter sales last year for this U.S. company."; "Once Malaysian and Singaporean officials began cracking down on chip smuggling this summer, Megaspeed stopped ordering from Nvidia."
excluded_implications: Any finding that Megaspeed or NVIDIA broke any law
That the two-percent figure is accurate
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The letter relays newspaper reporting; it is primary evidence only that the allegation was public.

claims.assertion: Conditional arithmetic only: if the relayed 'nearly two percent' referred to FY2025 Data Center revenue ($115,186m), it would correspond to roughly $2.3bn.
claims.pinpoint: Derived from SI1-C-19 and FY2025 Data Center revenue
claims.scope: Hypothetical sizing of an S2 claim
excluded_implications: Any reliance on the figure as a finding
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The base ('worldwide datacenter sales last year') is ambiguous; classed S2 because the input is S2.

claims.assertion: Across two-session windows [0,+1] around six earlier public signals, NVDA's cumulative abnormal return was insignificant in four (three negative, one positive) and significantly negative (|t|>2 against both SMH and SPY models) in two: 14–15 Oct 2025 (after the Senator letter; −5.3% vs both models) and 26–27 Feb 2026 (FY2026 results/10-K; −5.3% vs SMH, −7.4% vs SPY). Neither move is attributable to the paired document on this evidence.
excluded_implications: That any price move was caused by the paired disclosure
That the market had or had not priced the diversion risk
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Windows contain other news (earnings, tariff and macro headlines) not controlled for; SMH contains NVDA.

errata.correction: SI1-C-21 called two windows 'significantly negative (|t|>2 against both SMH and SPY models)'. That used per-test thresholds across 24 tests (6 events × 2 windows × 2 benchmarks). With a Bonferroni-adjusted two-sided 5% threshold (|t| > 3.08), only 14–15 Oct 2025 vs SMH (t = −3.10) and 26–27 Feb 2026 vs SPY (t = −3.11) exceed it, each marginally. 'Significant' should read 'nominally significant; marginal after multiple-comparison adjustment'.
errata.reason: The original text already declined to attribute either move to the paired document; the correction weakens the statistics further, in the same direction.

errata.correction: SI1-SRC-014 (MHA transcript, 3 March 2025) was found on 2026-11-15 at a new URL (https://www.mha.gov.sg/media-room/newsroom/transcript-of-media-conference-with-mr-k-shanmugam-minister-for-home-affairs-and-minister-for-law-regarding-the-case-involving-the-three-men-who-were-charged-on-27-february-2025-for-fraud-by-false-representation/), through a link in a post-event document (SI1-PST-013). It stays EXCLUDED from the pre-event inference. The discovery path is post-event, and pre-cutoff availability rests only on the date shown on the page plus a web-archive index entry for the former URL (capture timestamp 2025-05-28) whose content was not retrieved. Its content is used only in POST_EVENT_VALIDATION.md.
errata.reason: The pre-event findings are not strengthened; the document is assessed after the fact as material a blind analyst could have obtained.

errata.correction: For government documents, availability_utc was set to the end of the official document date, or to PDF metadata time. These values show the document date or file creation, not demonstrated public accessibility. The availability_review addendum separates document date, official publication date, demonstrated availability and retrieval date. SI1-SRC-013 is rated insufficiently_demonstrated.
errata.reason: SI1-SRC-013 supports only S2 claims (SI1-C-19, SI1-C-20), which carry no findings. No S0 or S1 claim depends solely on a source rated insufficiently_demonstrated (machine-checked).

errata.correction: The pre-event event study used adjusted closes retrieved on 2026-11-15, i.e. a post-cutoff data vintage. Recomputing on unadjusted closes changed every pre-event CAR[0,+1] by at most 0.03 percentage points. Event windows were chosen by the researcher when the analysis was run; they were not pre-registered.
errata.reason: The vintage effect is negligible. Non-registered windows are a disclosed limitation.

errata.correction: SI1-E-01 used normal critical values (|t| > 3.08 for 24 tests) with t-statistics from an estimated market model, and concluded that two windows exceeded it. Under the documented inference (Student-t, df = 118, Bonferroni at 5% two-sided over 24 tests) the threshold is |t| > 3.148. The frozen statistics (−3.099 and −3.112) do not exceed it. Recomputed with n − 2 residual variance and estimation-error-adjusted CAR variance, they are −3.060 and −3.056 (Bonferroni p = 0.066 and 0.067; event-study-inference-correction.json). NO pre-event window is statistically significant after multiple-comparison adjustment. SI1-E-01's statement that two windows exceed the threshold is withdrawn.
errata.reason: The earlier statement about statistical significance is reversed: neither window is significant after adjustment. Observed returns are unchanged. The original pre-event text already declined causal attribution, so the substantive conclusion (no evidence that the market reacted to the paired disclosures) is unchanged or strengthened.

errata.correction: EVIDENCE_PROTOCOL.md §2 says a source whose pre-cutoff availability cannot be demonstrated is excluded from inference. SI1-SRC-013 is rated insufficiently_demonstrated but was admitted in the frozen register; that admission was inconsistent with the protocol. The frozen record is preserved. For any use, treat SI1-SRC-013 and the S2 claims SI1-C-19 and SI1-C-20 as carrying no evidential weight, beyond recording that a lead existed. SI1-SRC-008, -009, -011 and -012 are rated inferred_from_official_date: their existence and official dates are evidenced, but public availability before the cutoff is not demonstrated. The S0 claims SI1-C-15 to SI1-C-18 are therefore conditional on that inference. Under the unchanged criterion, P1 is NOT ESTABLISHED for MON-SI-001 (8 of 13 admitted sources demonstrated). The gate's P1 measurement column ('tools/check_registers.py passes on every case') was read in the first two passes as if structural checks satisfied the criterion. The criterion text governs and is not redefined. The checker now reports structural consistency separately from P1 status, and it fails if the gate reports P1 as satisfied while any admitted source lacks demonstrated availability.
errata.reason: The first and second passes described P1 as passing on the strength of the structural checker. That overstated it. Pre-event findings F4 (regulatory tightening) and F5 (named-intermediary lead) rest on the conditional or insufficient sources and are downgraded to conditional. F1–F3 and F6 rest on EDGAR filings (demonstrated) and are unaffected, except where they cite the Singapore MTI reply (SI1-C-15) as corroboration.

p1_assessment.what_would_establish_it: For each inferred source, an independent contemporaneous record (e.g. a web-archive capture dated before 2026-05-12, or a dated third-party citation), or exclusion of the source and its claims in a new, separately registered reconstruction. The frozen record is not edited.
